questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs show road rules that you must follow.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a way to prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking and keep them busy while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends involved in stopping your friend from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange a ride for them, keep them busy with other activities, and ask other friends for help. Waiting 15 minutes after drinking does not make someone safe to drive.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should not rely only on mirrors to see what's around them because:

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than the mirrors on other vehicles, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road in front of you and they should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles. You cannot see everything with mirrors alone. Turn your head frequently to check blind spots.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, you should:

options.text: Try to minimize the number of rest breaks.
Use artificial stimulants, like caffeine, if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to avoid getting too cold during the ride.
Schedule more than 12 hours of riding a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to avoid getting too cold during the ride.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine, as fatigue will hit hard when they wear off.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Ride with extra caution at intersections.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
If a load is too high, it may interfere with the turn signals.
It may be difficult to see over a load that is placed too high.
Others can't see your load if it is low.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes the bike harder to balance.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than you usually would.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance at night. Slow down and stay further back from other vehicles. Use your high beam unless you are meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance when following another vehicle at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance when following another vehicle at night.
You should always maintain the same following distance regardless of the time of day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance when following another vehicle at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see at night. You cannot see shadows or light contrasts that help you judge distance during the day. Allow more space between you and other vehicles at night.

questions.question: Bright-colored helmets:

options.text: Help other drivers see you better.
Do not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: A bright-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects your head in a crash and makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing together.

questions.explanation: When riders pass another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider starts.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Rain suits should:

options.text: Not puff up or balloon when you ride.
Not be needed since motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not puff up or balloon when you ride.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits for motorcycles will not tear or balloon when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Before riding, check everything except:

options.text: The condition of the tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread depth, and the condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.question: When riding at night, do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight except when a vehicle is ahead of or coming toward you.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, safely exit the road and check your tires.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake hard and slowly increase front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. Speed up to pass or slow down to drop back.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it is free of damage.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards and fit snugly. It must be free of damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a good view of scenery.
Keep you hidden in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide what you plan to do next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay safe. Position yourself to avoid blind spots, be seen by others, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and have an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide good wind protection.
